title: Klaus and the postman.
lines: Once upon a time there was a young man called Jesper.
His father was the boss of all the postmen in the country.
Jesper was rich and a bit lazy.
He would rather lie in his soft bed than work.
One day his father said: Jesper, it's time you learned something.
You're going to be a postman.
In a little town, all the way up north.
It's called Smeerensburg.
And you have to send six thousand letters there in one year.
Otherwise you can't come back.
Smeerensburg was on a cold island full of snow.
It was grey and dark.
The people weren't friendly.
They were always arguing.
Two families had been fighting each other for hundreds of years.
They threw snowballs and fish.
The children didn't go to school.
And nobody ever wrote a letter.
Jesper sighed.
Six thousand letters?
Nobody here writes even one letter!
One day Jesper walked far away, outside the town.
There, deep in the forest, stood a big wooden house.
A big, quiet man with a long white beard lived there.
His name was Klaus.
Klaus lived alone.
He was a woodcutter.
But in his house there were lots and lots of toys.
Wooden toys, that he had made himself.
Little trains, little ducks, dolls.
Why do you make all those toys?
asked Jesper.
Klaus didn't say anything.
He looked a little sad.
Later Jesper heard the story.
Klaus and his wife had really wanted children.
But they never had any.
When his wife died, Klaus was left alone with all the toys.
One day Jesper found a drawing.
A child had made a drawing of themselves, looking very sad.
Jesper took one of Klaus's toys to that child.
Secretly, at night, down the chimney.
The next morning the child was so happy.
They told all the other children.
And then the children all wrote letters.
To Klaus!
Dear Klaus, may I have a toy too?
Jesper was happy.
Letters!
He had to deliver them!
He helped Klaus.
Every night they drove through the town in a sleigh.
Klaus wore a red coat, because it was cold.
They went in down the chimney.
They left the toys in the houses.
And they left again, before anyone woke up.
But there was a problem.
Klaus didn't have enough toys for everyone.
So Jesper told the children: Klaus only gives toys to good children.
And then something changed.
The children became kind.
They helped their mummies and daddies.
They stopped arguing.
They wanted to learn to write, so they could send letters.
There was a school again.
A teacher taught them to read and write.
And the mummies and daddies?
They saw how kind their children were.
They started being kind too.
They said good morning to each other.
They helped each other.
Even the two families who had always been fighting had dinner together.
Smeerensburg became a warm, happy town, with lights and music.
By the end of the year Jesper had delivered more than six thousand letters.
He could go back home.
To his soft bed.
But Jesper didn't want to leave anymore.
He stayed in Smeerensburg.
Because he had friends here.
And here he had learned how lovely it is to give something.
Every year, on the same winter night, Jesper and Klaus drove around in the sleigh to bring toys.
After a while Klaus grew old.
And one night, in the snow, he disappeared.
Nobody knows where.
But every year, on that winter night, Jesper sees a sleigh in the sky.
With a man in a red coat and a long white beard.
And the children still get toys.
Do you know what that man is called now?
The end.
